\[
E = \lvert \nabla (G_\sigma * Y) \rvert,
\qquad
M = \operatorname{HMIN}_h(E),
\qquad
h = 10
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(E\): The elevation, the gradient magnitude
- \(G_\sigma * Y\): The luma after a Gaussian blur
- \(\operatorname{HMIN}_h\): The minima at least h deep

The elevation E is the gradient magnitude of the blurred luma Y, so edges are ridges and flat areas are valleys. Every regional minimum would start its own region, and noise makes very many of them. The h-minima transform keeps only the minima at least h deep: a dip whose floor is less than h below the lowest pass out of it does not count. Each kept minimum, as a connected set of pixels, becomes a marker. The h-minima transform would count every minimum that ties exactly with the lowest elevation, however shallow, so this filter first breaks exact ties by adding at most 1e-6, our choice. Then water rises from all markers at once, in order of elevation. Each pixel joins the flood that reaches it first, and floods from different markers meet along the ridges, which become the boundaries.
